unit.title: Teaching databases and data engineering at university

video.title: Data quality and project assessment: Validation, lineage and real datasets
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Charts draw themselves; code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Prof Farah - head of department, Amman
Dr Amina Bello - lecturer in education, Lagos
Narrator - the Darsi voice, talking to a university lecturer (warm, collegial, precise)

scenes.narration: The faculty's enrolment report shows a hundred and twelve percent attendance in one course. The query was correct. The data was not: some students were loaded twice. Who should have caught it?
Today: how bad data breaks good systems, how to test data like code, and how to assess student database projects built on real, messy datasets.
Data quality means fitness for use. Common dimensions are completeness, validity, uniqueness, consistency, accuracy and timeliness. Each can be tested automatically.
Write checks that run every time data is loaded. Keys must be unique, required fields not null, and values within range. A failing check stops the pipeline before the report is built.
Better still, let the database refuse bad data. A primary key on student and course would have rejected the duplicate load. Constraints are quality checks the database enforces for free.

Lineage records where each table came from and what transformed it. Datasheets describe how a dataset was collected and its known limits. Together they let someone else trust, or question, the numbers.

Clean textbook datasets hide the hardest part of the job. Give students a real, messy public dataset. Grade the schema, the quality checks and a written account of every cleaning decision, not just the final queries.
Quick check! Some students were loaded twice. Which quality dimension failed?
Uniqueness. Each student and course pair should appear once. A uniqueness test or a primary key would have caught it at load time.
In the app, open the quality lab. Run checks on a messy table, find the duplicates, gaps and impossible values, and decide how to handle each.
Your turn. Two student projects return identical final answers. What best distinguishes the stronger one?
The quality checks and the written justification of each cleaning decision. Remember: quality is testable, constraints enforce it, and documentation lets others trust the result.

scenes.on_screen_text: Try it in your next lecture
scenes.narration: Try it in your next lecture: hand out a public dataset with planted problems. Groups write three quality checks and run them. Then each group presents one cleaning decision and defends it.

checkpoints.prompt: Some students were loaded twice. Which quality dimension failed?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: each student and course pair should appear once.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: nothing was missing or late; rows were duplicated.

checkpoints.prompt: Two projects give identical answers. What best distinguishes the stronger one?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: the process shows whether the answers can be trusted.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: size isn't quality; checks and reasoning are.
